The free Poissonized walk has a fractional characteristic-function cusp and a monotone lattice heat kernel, so the lattice Tauberian theorem gives the normalized local tail. The killed image formula telescopes to exactly 2m free sites, fixing the survivor-tail constant without subtracting two uncontrolled equivalents. Tail integration and an independent killed-generator computation verify all moment boundaries. The first-passage mean transition is explicitly borrowed only in the Mittag-Leffler subfamily. value.rationale: The exact leading coefficient and exponent determine rare surviving positions at fixed experimental time for a motivated stochastic-search model. The q-moment cutoff is a natural risk/uncertainty observable, and its strict incompatibility with finite mean first passage in the Mittag-Leffler family gives a genuine structural trade-off. It is neither a finite parameter recomputation nor a bare transform substitution; extracting the tail requires a Tauberian argument and reflected-window normalization.
